name: Dandami Maria
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: van der Hulst, Harry, Rob Goedemans & Ellen van Zanten (eds.) 2010. A Survey of Word Accentual Patterns in the Languages of the World. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. Ch. 10 (Goedemans & van der Hulst), 'Word accent systems in the languages of Asia', pp. 569-570.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Dandami Maria appears only in the genealogical list of the Gondi group (p. 569); the Gondi statement (p. 570) is second-hand and about another variety: 'Steever (1998a: 274) characterizes accent in Gondi as non-phonemic and word-initial.' Not a statement about Dandami Maria.

sources.citation: Pandey, Keshinath M. 1979. A Grammar of Dandami Maria. Ph.D. thesis (supervisor R. C. Mehrotra), Department of Linguistics and Languages, Ravishankar University, Raipur. 287 pp. [Glottolog 423439, listed by Glottolog as a grammar]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 1 Phonology (pp. 15-62) lists 'twenty-four segmental and five suprasegmental phonemes'; the suprasegmentals are length /:/, open juncture, pause and the two terminal contours /./ and /?/ (pp. 15, 27; contrasts p. 39). Syllable section (pp. 39-45) gives structure and types only. The words 'stress' and 'accent' do not occur anywhere in the scanned text of the 287-page thesis (a full-text search for stress/accent over all 14 files).

sources.citation: Abidi, Shammi (dir.) & Rupendra Kavi (comp.) 2022. Hindi-Gondi (Dandami Madiya boli) shabdkosh evam vartalap sankshepika [Hindi-Gondi (Dandami Maria dialect) dictionary and conversation digest]. Nava Raipur: Tribal Research and Training Institute, Chhattisgarh. (Hindi)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing: preface on the dialect's area and speakers, then Hindi-Gondi wordlist and phrasebook in Devanagari; no phonology, no accent marks.

sources.citation: Subrahmanyam, P. S. 1983. Dravidian Comparative Phonology. Annamalainagar: Annamalai University.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative only: accent appears as historical accent-shift/stress-displacement hypotheses (Subbayya, Tuttle, Krishnamurti); Hill-Maria is cited for consonants; nothing about stress placement in Dandami Maria.

sources.citation: Grigson, W. V. 1938. The Maria Gonds of Bastar. London: Oxford University Press. Appendix on language and Hill Maria specimens, pp. 320-323.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; orthography/pronunciation notes (vowel length, a medial 'check', gutturals) and the statement 'I have not collected any specimens of Bison-horn Maria language, nor have I the qualifications to attempt any sketch of the grammars of the two dialects' (p. 323).

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.) 1906. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IV: Munda and Dravidian Languages (Dravidian part by Sten Konow). Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Gondi section incl. the 'so-called Maria of Bastar' specimen and notes, pp. 529-535.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library, call number 3254.1 F; Linguistics Library, call number CoPh 5.40; a Harvard library, call number Ud 0010
sources.note: No accent statement in the Gondi/Maria section (a full-text search for stress/accent that section for accent/stress/syllable: none); the only 'accent rests on the first syllable' sentence in the volume is in the Kanarese sketch (p. 871). Pandey 1979 (p. 8) calls the LSI Maria specimen unauthentic and its grammatical notes misleading.

sources.citation: Garapati, Uma Maheshwar Rao. 2008. A comparative grammar of the Gondi dialects: with special reference to phonology and morphology. Kuppam: Dravidian University. xxii+346+xviii pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Only phonology-focused work whose stated coverage includes South Bastar Gondi (= Dandami Maria) alongside the other Gondi dialects; a comparative phonology of this scope would normally carry an accent/stress paragraph, possibly per dialect.

sources.citation: Steever, Sanford B. 1998. Gondi. In Sanford B. Steever (ed.), The Dravidian Languages, 270-300. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Source behind the StressTyp/van der Hulst et al. 2010 line that Gondi accent is 'non-phonemic and word-initial' (p. 274); describes a different Gondi variety (Adilabad/Southern Gondi), so at best a sister-variety proxy, not a Dandami Maria statement.

sources.citation: Dutt, Kirtilata. 1969. Studies in the language and literature of some of the non-Aryan tribes of the Madhya Pradesh (Linguistic studies of Gondi, Dhurwa and Dorli). Ph.D. thesis, Ravishankar University, Raipur.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Per Pandey 1979 (pp. 10-12) contains a brief phonological account of Dandami Maria (as 'Gondi') from Faraspal near Dantewada; an independent phonology of the variety that might treat stress. Not on Shodhganga.

sources.citation: Burrow, Thomas & Sudhibhushan Bhattacharya. 1960. A comparative vocabulary of the Gondi dialects. Journal of the Asiatic Society (Calcutta) 2: 73-251.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Includes Dandami Maria data with a phonological introduction to the dialects (pp. 75-76 cited by Subrahmanyam 1983); could contain a remark on accent across Gondi dialects.
